8. ISSUE No.1: The petitioners contended that on 06.10.2023 at about 10.30 p.m. deceased Sasikumar Ragu met with road traffic accident due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-07-TA-9779 and Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-07-TA-9898.

The petitioner No.1 in order to establish their case filed the affidavit in lieu of chief examination of PW-1 and reiterated the petition averments and got marked the documents at Exs.P.1 to 20.
10. Negligence is a specific tort and in any given circumstances, the failure to exercise that care which the circumstances demand, where there is a duty to exercise care, reasonable care must be taken to avoid acts or omissions which can be reasonably foreseen to be likely to cause physical injury to persons or property.
In order to succeed in an action for damages/ compensation for breach, the aggrieved must establish breach of statutory duty which on the construction of the statute.

It is well settled that, those who claim negligence have to prove on the probabilities, as to whether breach or negligence, has caused or materially contributed to the damage suffered by the claimant/s.
11.
The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.
In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.

12. The burden is upon the petitioners to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving of the driver of the tractor bearing Reg. No. KA-23-TA-9779 and Trailer bearing Registration No.KA-07-TA-9898.

sentences.text: The culpable negligence or rashness can be inferred from the attending circumstances like time of the accident, the width of the road and the nature of road etc.
The Ex.P.4 is the spot Mahazar and Ex-P5 is the sketch prepared by the Investigating Agency in the presence of pancha/ witnesses.
The Bangalore- Chennai road is national Highway.
According to the claimants, the deceased was proceeding infront of shamil near Nagli Flower Mandi on Bangalore-Chennai Highway on left side.
So, the deceased was riding his bicycle on the extreme left side of the road.

It is not in dispute that,
the tractor driver did not hit the motor cycle from the front side.

As per charge-sheet at Ex.P3, FIR and First Information Statement i.e., Ex.P1 and Ex.P2, the driver of the tractor drove his tractor with trailer in rash and negligent manner and suddenly entered to highway as a result deceased was unable to control his motorcycle and dashed to the rear side of the tractor.
The driver of the tractor expected to exercise due care and skill in order to avoid the accident.
But, instead, it appears that, he straight away entered to the main road.
This amounts to negligent act.
The road was straight enough at that point and the driver of the tractor had clear vision of the oncoming and ongoing vehicles on the main highway.
If the tractor had been driven in a reasonable or moderate speed while enter to the main highway, definitely the driver would have averted the mishap.

Driver/rider is expected to drive/ride vehicle especially on road like this in such a way that he must be able to stop his vehicle at the short notice and he must stop the tractor before entering the high way.
A vehicle entering a highway from other road has duty to yield to traffic already on the highway.
But the tractor driver has not done so.
On perusing the Ex.P.1 to 3, it becomes clear that, the tractor driver was riding it in a rash and negligent manner.
As a result, the deceased died on account of fatal injuries sustained by him in the accident.
There is no reason to disbelieve records prepared by the police officials while discharging their duty.

Therefore, having regard to the documents produced by the petitioners, an inference is possible to draw that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent manner of driving of the t r a c t o r by its driver and in that accident, Sasikumar Ragu met with an accident and succumbed to it.
Further, the respondent No.1 has not adduced any rebuttal evidence to disbelieve the case as set forth by the petitioners.

19. The respondent No.1 has not stepped into the witness box to rebut the evidence of petitioners and to support the defence taken up in the written statement that the deceased also contributed his own negligence towards the occurrence of the accident in question.

In the light of not entering into witness box an adverse inference will have to be drawn as contemplated Under Sec.114 (g) of the Indian Evidence Act that the defence taken in the written statement is not true and correct.

Facts of the above cases and facts of the present case in hands are altogether are different.

As such,

In this case, as per the charge sheet tractor suddenly entered to the main road i.e., National Highway.

23. The petitioner No.1 is the father and petitioner No.2 is the mother of the deceased.
Fact to be noted here that petitioners are none other than the parents of the deceased is not seriously disputed by the contesting respondent.

Even there is no material on record to show this dependent has independent income of their own and thereby not depended on deceased at all, the deceased out of his income contributed to the income of family consisting of himself and petitioners herein.

Hence,
it is clear that, all the petitioners are depending upon the income of the deceased Sasikumar Ragu.
Since, the deceased is bachelor 1/2 of the income should be taken towards personal expenses of the deceased.

An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation".
So 40% of future prospects is taken into consideration.
Taking into consideration of the same, if 40% is added to the income of the deceased it would be Rs.24,401/- + 40% (Rs.9,760/-) = Rs.34,161/- per month.
Since, the deceased is bachelor 50% has to be deducted towards personal expenses.

Therefore the annual income (Rs. 17,080 x 12) is Rs.2,04,960/-.
As such correct multiplier as per guidelines of Sarala Varma case would be "17".

In which it is held in para No.8.7 that:
"A constitution bench of this court in pranay sethi (supra) dealt with the various heads under which the compensation it so be awarded in a death case.
One of these heads is "Loss of consortium".
In legal parlance "consortium" is a compendious term which encompasses spousal consortium; parental consortium and filial consortium.

The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance,
solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.
With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse.

Spouse consortium is generally defined as rights pertaining to the relationship of a husband-wife which allows compensation to the surviving spouse for loss of "company", society, co- operation, affection and aid of the other in every conjugal relation".
Parental consortium is granted to the child upon the premature death of a parent, for loss of "parental aid, protection, affection, society, discipline, guidance and training".
Filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.
An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose their child during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their oral in the family unit.
Consortium is a special prism reflection changing norms about the status and worth of actual relationship.
Modern jurisdictional world-over have recognized that the value further on perusal of child's consortium far exceeds the economic value of the compensation awarded in case of death of a child.
Most jurisdictions therefore permit parents to be awarded compensation under loss of consortium on the death of a child.
The amount awarded to the parents is a compensating for loss of love, affection, care and companionship of the deceased child.
29. The petitioner No.1 is the father of the deceased and petitioner No.2 is the mother of the deceased

, so they are entitled for consortium for loss of "protection, affection, society, discipline,
guidance and training".
Therefore, Rs.40,000/- each is awarded to the petitioners No.1 and respondent No.3 under the head of loss of consortium.

31. LIABILITY:

As discussed in issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Tractor bearing Reg. No. KA-07-TA-9779 and Trailer bearing Reg.
No.KA-07-TA-9898 and the police have conducted due inquiry and filed charge sheet against the driver of said offending vehicle.
On perusal of the policy, the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.1 for the period from 07.03.2023 to 06.03.2024.
Admittedly, the accident in question took place on 06.10.2023.
Hence, policy was inforce as on the date of accident.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, respondent No.1 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2 owner.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following issues:

:REASONS:
8. ISSUE No.1: The petitioners contended that on 06.10.2023 at about 10.30 p.m. deceased Sasikumar Ragu met with road traffic accident due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-07-TA-9779 and Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-07-TA-9898.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In order to succeed in an action for damages/ compensation for breach, the aggrieved must establish breach of statutory duty which on the construction of the statute.
It is well settled that, those who claim negligence have to prove on the probabilities, as to whether breach or negligence, has caused or materially contributed to the damage suffered by the claimant/s.
11.
The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.
In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.
17. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL)
The culpable negligence or rashness can be inferred from the attending circumstances like time of the accident, the width of the road and the nature of road etc.
A vehicle entering a highway from other road has duty to yield to traffic already on the highway.
As a result, the deceased died on account of fatal injuries sustained by him in the accident.
There is no reason to disbelieve records prepared by the police officials while discharging their duty.
Therefore, having regard to the documents produced by the petitioners, an inference is possible to draw that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent manner of driving of the t r a c t o r by its driver and in that accident, Sasikumar Ragu met with an accident and succumbed to it.
Further, the respondent No.1 has not adduced any rebuttal evidence to disbelieve the case as set forth by the petitioners.
19. The respondent No.1 has not stepped into the witness box to rebut the evidence of petitioners and to support the defence taken up in the written statement that the deceased also contributed his own negligence towards the occurrence of the accident in question.
In the light of not entering into witness box an adverse inference will have to be drawn as contemplated Under Sec.114 (g) of the Indian Evidence Act that the defence taken in the written statement is not true and correct.
Hence question of contributory negligence and maintaining safe distance by the deceased motor cyclist does not arise at all.
Hence, the income of the deceased is the Tribunal has to consider the future prospects on actual salary less tax and even for self employed or were engaged on fixed wages.
The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance,
solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.
With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse.
Spouse consortium is generally defined as rights pertaining to the relationship of a husband-wife which allows compensation to the surviving spouse for loss of "company", society, co- operation, affection and aid of the other in every conjugal relation".
Parental consortium is granted to the child upon the premature death of a parent, for loss of "parental aid, protection, affection, society, discipline, guidance and training".
Filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.
An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose their child during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their oral in the family unit.
Consortium is a special prism reflection changing norms about the status and worth of actual relationship.
Most jurisdictions therefore permit parents to be awarded compensation under loss of consortium on the death of a child.
The amount awarded to the parents is a compensating for loss of love, affection, care and companionship of the deceased child.
, so they are entitled for consortium for loss of "protection, affection, society, discipline,
guidance and training".
